title: Untouchable

vibeProfile.oneLine: A day in the life of a young untouchable in colonial India.

summary: A single day in the life of Bakha, a young latrine cleaner in colonial India, follows him through the humiliations heaped on him because of his caste, and the small hopes that might offer a way out. Mulk Raj Anand's pioneering novel was one of the first in English to put an untouchable at its centre and to attack the cruelty of caste head-on. Spare, angry and humane, it remains a landmark of Indian social fiction and a searing portrait of dignity under daily contempt.
whyReadIt: A landmark Indian novel that put an untouchable at its centre and attacked caste head-on. Spare, angry and humane.

funFacts.text: It was among the first Indian novels in English to confront caste oppression directly.
